reference_title: Assuring Quality in Geotechnical Reporting Documents
chapter_title: Considerations in Development of Geotechnical Reporting Documents

sections.title: Introduction: Alternative Delivery Methods and QA Roles
sections.summary: Each GRD involves four roles: (1) GRD preparer; (2) QC reviewer (independent check of technical details); (3) QA reviewer (confirms QC was done; broader project view); (4) QA auditor (verifies QA reviews have been completed; need not be GS). These four individuals should generally be different people. Seven ADMs cover all ACMs: Methods 1-4 for DBB, CM/GC, and DB preliminary (owner staff, design consultant, GS subconsultant, GS direct); Methods 5-7 for DB final design (contractor's GS team). QC reviewers verify technical accuracy; QA reviewers verify QC was done and recommendations fit the overall project.
sections.body:
ACMs and ADMs: DBB is traditional (100% design before bid). DB is popular for reducing project delivery time; design at ~30% when contractor proposals are solicited; final design and construction by DB Team. CM/GC is less common but allows close owner-designer-contractor coordination; owner maintains full design control; contractor provides constructability input during design.

Four participants in GRD QA: (1) GRD preparer — develops the GRD; (2) QC reviewer — must understand technical details of calculations, exploration logs, lab test results; confirms accuracy; (3) QA reviewer — maintains broader project view; confirms appropriate QC has been completed and recommendations appropriately address risks; (4) QA auditor — verifies QA reviews have been conducted; does not need to be a GS.

Seven ADMs: Methods 1-4 (used for DBB, DB preliminary, and CM/GC): (1) owner agency in-house GS; (2) design consultant with in-house GS; (3) design consultant with GS subconsultant; (4) GS consultant directly to owner. Methods 5-7 (DB final design after contract award, GS under contractor): (5) contractor with design consultant having in-house GS; (6) contractor with design consultant using GS subconsultant; (7) contractor directly with GS consultant.

QC vs QA difference: QC reviewers confirm and document accuracy of technical efforts; QA reviewers confirm and document that appropriate QC has been completed.
key_points: Four GRD participants: preparer, QC reviewer (technical details), QA reviewer (process verifier), QA auditor (program verifier)
QC reviewer checks technical accuracy; QA reviewer confirms QC was done; auditor checks the system
7 ADMs: Methods 1-4 for owner-side delivery; Methods 5-7 for DB final design (contractor's GS)

sections.title: DBB, DB, and CM/GC Roles, Responsibilities, and Communications
sections.summary: DBB: Owner provides requirements; consultant performs investigation, develops recommendations, verifies incorporation in PS&E. DB: Owner prepares GDR for bid phase to reduce risk; DB Team's GS performs final design investigation after award; interim GRDs allowed per construction schedule; over-the-shoulder reviews required. CM/GC: similar to DBB QA; contractor reviews preliminary design and proposes modifications. All ACMs: scoping meeting at project start; periodic coordination meetings with minutes; GRD review meetings with design engineers.
sections.body:
DBB roles and responsibilities:
Owner: provide minimum investigation requirements; provide design standards and specifications; provide QA requirements and verify via audits. Consultant: understand project scope and geotechnical needs; perform investigation and analyses; develop recommendations with details and specifications; verify incorporation in PS&E; perform and document QC and QA reviews. Contractor: familiarize with GRDs; construct per plans and specifications; notify owner of variations from anticipated conditions.

DB roles and responsibilities:
Owner: provide minimum investigation requirements; provide technical provisions and performance requirements; provide GDR with factual data for bid phase (reduces risk and conservatism in bids); provide QA requirements for DB Team's final design GRDs; incorporate over-the-shoulder review meetings into schedule. Consultant (owner-side, preliminary design): develop GDR for bid phase. Consultant (DB Team, final design): review GDR; if selected, perform final design investigation; develop final design GRDs; develop or implement QA plan. Contractor: coordinate with design consultant throughout; require GRDs before construction begins; notify GS of variations in conditions.

CM/GC roles and responsibilities: Similar to DBB for design side. Contractor engaged by owner to review preliminary plans and recommend modifications. Interim GRDs address contractor-proposed scheme evaluations. Owner maintains full design and QA control.

Communications — all ACMs: scoping meeting to establish level of effort; periodic coordination meetings between owner, project designer, and GS; review of GRDs by owner and design engineers; minutes of meetings documenting discussions. DB adds: owner pre-bid meeting with proposers; over-the-shoulder meetings during final design; communication during construction for design-construction interface.
key_points: DBB: consultant verifies recommendations incorporated in PS&E; owner audits QA
DB: owner prepares GDR for bid phase; more GDR scope = less risk premium in bids
DB: over-the-shoulder reviews required — regular meetings between owner and contractor DB Team
DB final design: aggressive schedule; interim GRDs per construction element/segment allowed
All ACMs: scoping meeting + periodic coordination meetings + GRD review meetings with minutes
sections.applicability: Roles, responsibilities, and communication requirements for GRD development in all ACMs
